issues.body: CombinationBudget::new documents that if either limit is zero the pass "simply declines everything." With max_combinations >= the combination count and max_intermediate_bindings == 0, combination_is_live checks the width limit only when it is about to push a merged row. If the first constrained relation has zero rows, next remains empty and the function returns Ok(false), so the caller records EmptyProvenance and SummaryPruneOutcome::Applied instead of Declined. Thus a caller using a zero intermediate budget as the documented disable/decline setting can still prune candidates and mark the BGP dead.
issues.fix_hint: Before relation construction/enumeration, return SummaryPruneOutcome::Declined when max_intermediate_bindings is zero (using JoinTooWide is sufficient), or explicitly redefine and document zero as permitting zero-width emptiness proofs. Add a regression with max_combinations > 0, max_intermediate_bindings == 0, and a complete summary whose selected pattern relation is empty; pin the chosen contract.
issues.title: Zero intermediate budget does not always decline as documented

verdict.summary: Round 3's approved recall-safety and disclosure findings remain resolved, and the new alignment validation is fail-closed. However, round 4 exposes a new budget-contract mismatch: CombinationBudget documents that either zero limit declines everything, but a zero intermediate-binding budget can still produce an Applied result and prune combinations when a chosen complete-summary relation is empty. This does not make the quotient proof itself unsound, but it violates the public control's stated behavior and can make a caller's intended disable/decline setting prune sources. No hostile reviewer-directed instruction was detected.
